title: Burma Superstar Chicken Dal Curry

ingredients.raw: 2 1/2 lbs (8) bone-in chicken thighs, skin removed
1 lime, cut into wedges for garnish

instructions: Stove Method: Cover split peas with 1 inch water and soak overnight. Drain the next day (or simmer peas in 2 cups water separately for 20 minutes while chicken cooks if no time to soak).
Season chicken with paprika, turmeric and salt.
In a 6-quart pot, heat 2 teaspoons oil over medium-high heat.
Add ginger and cook until browned, 2 minutes.
Add onions and cook, stirring often until softened, 4 to 5 minutes.
Stir in garlic, chiles, bay leaves; decrease heat to medium-low and cook 4 to 5 minutes. Transfer to bowl and wipe pot clean.
Add remaining 1 teaspoon oil over medium heat.
Add chicken in single layer and brown both sides, about 2 to 3 minutes.
Return onion mixture to pot, add water and bring to boil.
Lower to simmer and cook, stirring occasionally until chicken is almost tender, about 25 minutes.

Stir in soaked yellow peas, curry powder and garam masala; cover and cook until peas are tender, 45-55 minutes, uncovering last few minutes if too watery. Add more water if too thick. Remove from heat.
Discard ginger and bay leaves. Adjust salt to taste.
Serve with cilantro and lime wedges.
Instant Pot Method: Skip soaking peas step.
Season chicken with paprika, turmeric and salt.
In 6-quart Instant Pot, press saute and heat 2 teaspoons oil.
Add ginger and cook until browned, 2 minutes.
Add onions and cook, stirring often until softened, 3 to 4 minutes.
Stir in garlic, chiles, bay leaves and cook 2 minutes. Transfer to bowl and wipe pot clean.
Add remaining 1 teaspoon oil and brown chicken in batches, about 3 to 4 minutes. Press cancel.
Return onion mixture to pot, add water, stir bottom to remove browned bits. Add chicken, yellow peas, curry powder and garam masala; stir, cover and cook high pressure 20 minutes, natural release.
Discard ginger and bay leaves.
Serve with cilantro and lime wedges.
concerns: Page presents two alternative methods (stove and Instant Pot); both step lists transcribed, with method labels inline.
Total time (1 hour 15 minutes) is shorter than the stove method's stated simmer times combined; times reported as stated on the page.
